description: Kung Pao Chicken is a beloved Szechuan dish featuring tender chicken pieces tossed with crunchy peanuts, fiery dried chilies, and a savory-sweet-spicy sauce. This classic Chinese stir-fry is renowned for its complex flavor profile and delightful texture contrasts. Its a perfect choice for a quick and satisfying lunch or dinner that truly delivers on taste.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the cubed chicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, and 1 teaspoon sesame oil. Mix well to coat all chicken pieces evenly. Let it marinate for at least 15 minutes while you prepare other ingredients.

instructions.title: Prepare the Kung Pao Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons Chinkiang vinegar, 1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine, 1 tablespoon sugar, 1 tablespoon cornstarch, and 2 tablespoons chicken broth until smooth. Set aside.

instructions.title: Stir-fry Aromatics and Chilies
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant and the chilies darken slightly. Be careful not to burn them.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the marinated chicken to the wok in a single layer. Let it sear for 1-2 minutes without moving, then stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned on all sides, about 3-5 minutes. Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.

instructions.title: Add Garlic, Ginger, and Green Onions
instructions.text: Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil to the wok if needed. Add the minced garlic, minced ginger, and the white and light green parts of the sliced green onions. Stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the wok. Give the prepared Kung Pao sauce a quick whisk again, then pour it over the chicken. Stir quickly to coat everything as the sauce thickens. Add the roasted peanuts and stir for another 30 seconds. Remove from heat immediately. Garnish with the chopped green parts of the green onions and serve hot.

tips: Do not overcrowd the wok when cooking the chicken; cook in batches if necessary to ensure it browns properly and cooks evenly.
For authentic flavor, do not skip the Sichuan peppercorns. They provide the unique 'mala' numbing sensation characteristic of Szechuan cuisine. Adjust the quantity to your spice preference.
Serve Kung Pao Chicken immediately over steamed white rice to best enjoy its vibrant flavors and textures. It does not store well for extended periods as the peanuts can lose their crispness.
